issues.description: Method name mismatch for Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient): The problem statement UML (and the solution implementation) declares a method Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template implementation provides a method named Stock.addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This naming inconsistency means student code or instructor-provided SealSaloon code that expects addToStockIngredients will not compile against the template (or students will be confused which name to use).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution: rename the template method public void addItem(StockIngredient ingredient) to public void addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient ingredient) (keeping the implementation and visibility). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use addItem and ensure the solution and SealSaloon code consistently use the same method name.

issues.description: The concept is adding a StockIngredient to the Stock collection. The problem statement (UML) names this operation addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). The template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). The solution Stock class uses addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient). This naming mismatch means students reading the UML/requirements will look for addToStockIngredients in the template but find addItem instead, increasing cognitive load and risking confusion about which method to call or implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) to match the UML and solution. Alternatively, add a new delegating method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in the template that calls addItem, preserving existing behavior while making the API match the problem statement.
